words.gram: pres. part. pass. vi-√bhid, acc. sg.

hindi: जो शष्कुली यानी सम्भवतः एक प्रकार की तली हुई टिकिया या अपूप यानी पुओं को खाकर या निगलकर जागने पर उलटी करता है; जिसके सिर पर लताएँ आदि उगती हैं और पक्षी आकर बैठ जाते हैं, या मौढ्य यानी मूढ़ता हो जाती है; जिसकी सेवा गिद्ध, उल्लू, कौए आदि से होती है, या प्रेत यानी मृतात्मा, पिशाच, राक्षस, द्रविड़, आन्ध्र, स्त्री, चण्डाल आदि से; या जिसे दक्षिण की ओर मुख किए हुए नाचती हुई स्त्री खींचती है, या कौए आदि खींचते हैं; या जो स्वयं दिगम्बर होकर निर्जन वन को जाता है, या वानर के रथ से; जिसे प्रेत या प्रव्रजित यानी संन्यासी गले लगाते हैं; या जो नग्न होकर लाल माला धारण करता है; कीचड़ से लिपटा हुआ हँसता या नाचता है; वेत्र यानी सम्भवतः बेंत, बाँस, काँटों और घास के घने झुरमुट में उलझ जाता है; या धूल को तकिया बनाई हुई भूमि पर गिरता है, या दीमक की बाँबी, राख, श्मशान, गड्ढों और निवासों में; या कीचड़, कुओं और गँदले जल में डूबता है, या धारा में बहा लिया जाता है; या लाल फूलों के वनों वाली भूमि, अँधेरे से भरी गुफा, बुरे कर्म के निवास, संकीर्ण स्थान या माता में प्रवेश करता है; या मछली से निगला जाता है; और जो श्मश्रु-कर्म यानी दाढ़ी का कर्म, शरीर की वृद्धि और विवाह का अनुभव करता है; जो अनुमानित पाठ पर पर्वत या महल की चोटी से गिरता है या चढ़ता है यूप यानी यज्ञ के खम्भों पर, फूलों से भरे हुओं पर, शाल्मली यानी सेमल पर, किंशुक यानी ढाक पर, कोविदार यानी सम्भवतः कचनार पर और पारिभद्रक यानी सम्भवतः फरहद पर; या जो हारता है, बाँधा जाता है, उलटी करता है, विरेचित होता है, प्रसन्न होता है, या सोना, लोहा, नमक, तेल, पिण्याक यानी खली और कपास पाता है; पका हुआ अन्न खाता है, मद्य यानी नशीला पेय या स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा पीता है, या लेप लगाया जाता है, या क्रुद्ध पितरों से डाँटा जाता है; या चन्द्र, सूर्य, तारा, दीपक, देवता, नेत्र और दाँतों में से किसी एक को नष्ट होता देखता है; या टेढ़े को, या बाँह को, या विदीर्ण होते हुए नग्न को देखता है; या नग्न, गेरुए रंग के वस्त्र पहने, असौम्य यानी उग्र, हाथ में दण्ड और पाश लिए, काले, लाल आँखों वाले पुरुषों को, या काली, श्वेत रूप वाली, लम्बे केश और स्तनों वाली, कालरात्रि के रूप वाली स्त्री को देखता है; वे रोगी पंचता यानी मृत्यु को प्राप्त होते हैं।
english: One who, having eaten or swallowed śaṣkulī (probably a kind of fried cake) or apūpa cakes, vomits on waking; on whose head creepers and the like grow and birds settle, or foolishness (mauḍhya) occurs; who is attended by vultures, owls, crows and the like, or by pretas (departed spirits), piśācas (flesh-eating demons), rakṣases (demons), Draviḍas, Āndhras, women, caṇḍālas (men of the lowest caste) and the like; or who, facing south, is dragged by a dancing woman, or by crows and the like; or who himself, naked (sky-clothed), goes to a deserted forest, or in a monkey-chariot; who is embraced by pretas or by renunciants (pravrajita); or who, naked, wears a red garland; who, smeared with mud, laughs or dances; who gets entangled in a thicket of vetra (probably cane), bamboo, thorns and grass; or who falls on ground that has dust for a pillow, or in anthills, ashes, cremation grounds, pits, abodes; or who sinks in mud, wells, turbid water, or is carried along by a current; or who enters a land with forests of red flowers, a cave filled with darkness, an abode of evil action, a confined place, or a mother; or who is swallowed by a fish; and who undergoes beard-work, growth of the body and marriage; who, on a conjectural reading, falls from the top of a mountain or palace, or climbs sacrificial posts, flower-rich (ones), śālmalī (silk-cotton tree), kiṃśuka (flame-of-the-forest), kovidāra (probably mountain ebony) and pāribhadraka (probably coral tree); or who is defeated, is bound, vomits, is purged, rejoices, or obtains gold, iron, salt, oil, oil-cake, cotton; eats cooked food, drinks madya (an intoxicating drink) or sneha (oil or fat); or is anointed, or is rebuked by angry forefathers; or sees any one of moon, sun, stars, lamp, deities, eyes, teeth perishing; or a crooked (thing), or an arm, or a naked (one) being split apart; or men who are naked, wearing ochre-coloured (kaṣāya) garments, fierce (asaumya, not gentle), with staff and noose in hand, black, red-eyed; or a woman who is black, of white appearance, with long hair and breasts, having the form of Kālarātri (dark night): they, being sick, attain pañcatā (lit. 'five-ness', death).

text_flags.why: certain: stray printed space before visarga-r (ādyai rvā = ādyaiḥ vā); fixed in words

possible: 'patya' is not a form that fits; 'patati ārohati' (falls … or climbs) gives sense and sandhi (patatyārohati) with one lost syllable ta; adopted on a conjectural reading and marked so in the translations
possible, NOT adopted: 'vakram vā bāhum' reads oddly (crooked … or arm); vaktram 'mouth, face' may be meant (kt/k loss); printed vakram kept in words and translation

notes: GROUPING: 35 and 36 appear to continue one sentence: 36 gives the contrast for the healthy (verb carried over). The whole unit is one long printed line with many yaḥ-clauses (each 'who …') and closes with 'te vyādhitāḥ pañcatām āpnuvanti'; the clauses are all marked by vā/ca, so the semicolons in the translation are an editorial division. Readings: 'abhyavahṛtya' = eating or swallowing (kept as in the glossary). 'chardayati' (vomits) and 'viricyate' (is purged, passive) kept distinct. 'srotasā' here is a water-current, not the body channel. 'dig-vāsāḥ' (sky-clothed) = naked. 'kapi-ratha' (monkey-chariot) relation of the compound is not stated. 'valmīka-…-āyatana': śvabhra-āyatana could also be one tat-puruṣa ('pit-abodes'); the dvandva list is taken. 'paṅka-kūpa-kaluṣa-udaka': could also be 'mud, well, turbid water' as three or four members; taken as a list. 'saṃbādha' read as noun 'confined place'; 'jananī' is 'mother' (a womb is not stated). 'śmaśru-karma' is literally beard-work (not further explained). 'yūpa-puṣpa-āḍhya-śālmalī-…': puṣpāḍhya (flower-rich) may qualify the following trees ('flower-rich śālmalī, …') instead of standing as a separate member; the plain list reading is taken. 'labhate vā hiraṇya…kārpāsān aśnāti pakvānnaṃ': taken as 'obtains gold…cotton; eats cooked food'. Alternatively aśnāti takes the whole list (eats gold, iron, salt, oil, oil-cake, cotton) as well as the cooked food; the sandhi 'kārpāsān aśnāti' allows both. 'daśana' in the series moon … eyes, teeth = teeth. 'anyatamān' is plural ('any of'); 'naśyataḥ' accusative plural participle. 'vakraṃ vā bāhuṃ nagnaṃ vā vibhidyamānaṃ': vibhidyamānam may agree with vakram, bāhum or nagnam; translated as printed (see text_flags). 'kaṣāya-vāsasaḥ': kaṣāya here is a colour (reddish-brown, ochre), not a taste (standard sense of the word). 'śukla-darśanā' = of white appearance; daśanā 'white-toothed' is a possible alternative, not adopted. 'dīrgha-keśa-stanīm': dīrgha may qualify hair only or hair and breasts. Kālarātri here = form of 'dark night'. 'pañcatā' = the euphemism for death. Identifications (modern names beside the Sanskrit): śālmalī = Bombax ceiba (standard). kiṃśuka = Butea monosperma, palāśa (standard). kovidāra = Bauhinia variegata (probable). pāribhadraka = Erythrina variegata (probable; the name is also used for other trees). vetra = cane, rattan, Calamus (probable). vaṃśa = bamboo (standard). kārpāsa = cotton, Gossypium (standard). śaṣkulī = a fried cake (probable; the word also means the ear-orifice, not here). Draviḍa and Āndhra are kept as names (in standard use peoples of the south). Print habits (recorded here once): b for v (bayāṃsi = vayāṃsi, prabrajita = pravrajita); a double avagraha ('' ) printed after -ā in ''kṛṣyate is a print habit, not an elision. Regular sandhi (digvāsā, pariṣvajyate nagno) needs no flag.

hindi: किन्तु स्वस्थ, जीवन के सन्देह को।
english: But the healthy (ones): a doubt about life.
notes: GROUPING: 36 appears to continue 35: the verb (āpnuvanti, 'attain') is carried over from 35 and is not supplied in the translation (elliptical line). The closing 'iti' ('thus') ends the statement begun in 35. 'svasthāḥ' is taken as the plural of the healthy (ones); 'jīvita-saṃdeham' as accusative, the object of the carried verb.

hindi: और यहाँ होते हैं।
english: And here there are.
notes: Lead-in formula 'bhavanti cātra' ('and here there are'), which in this treatise introduces the verses that follow (38 onward); nothing is supplied after 'bhavanti' in the translation.

hindi: मन को वहन करने वाले स्रोतस् यानी मार्गों के प्रबल मलों यानी अपशिष्ट से भरे होने के कारण
english: Because of the fullness of the mind-carrying channels (srotas) with powerful malas (waste matter),
notes: GROUPING: 38 and 39 appear to form one sentence (38 gives the reason, 39 the statement). 'srotas' (channel) and 'mala' (waste, impurity) are doctrinal terms and kept; whether mala here means the doṣas is not stated. 'manovaha' is taken as 'mind-carrying' (qualifying srotasām).

hindi: विनाश की ओर उन्मुख आत्मा वालों द्वारा भयंकर स्वप्न देखे जाते हैं।
english: Terrible dreams are seen by (ones) whose selves are turned toward destruction.
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence begun in 38. 'svapnā' = svapnāḥ (regular loss of visarga before v).

hindi: अशुभ स्वप्न को भी देखकर जो वहीं फिर से
english: One who, having seen even an inauspicious dream, right there again
notes: GROUPING: 40 and 41 form one sentence (the verb paśyet is in 41). 'tatra eva' is taken as 'right there' (in that very place or in that same sleep); the text does not say which.

hindi: सौम्य और शुभ को देखे, तो उसके लिए फल शुभ ही हो।
english: should see a gentle, auspicious (one), for him the result would be auspicious indeed.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 40. 'saumyam śubham' stand for an unstated noun (the dream is understood from 40), shown as '(one)'.

hindi: देवताओं को, द्विज यानी दो बार जन्म लेने वालों को, गायों और बैलों को, जीवित मित्रों को, राजाओं को
english: Gods (deva), twice-born (dvija), cows and bulls, living friends, kings,
notes: GROUPING: 42 to 45 are lists of accusatives with no verb in them; they appear to be objects of 'paśyet' in 46 (or continue 41). 'go-vṛṣabha' is taken as a dvandva 'cows and bulls'; 'bull (go-vṛṣabha)' as one word is also possible. 'suhṛdo nṛpān' = suhṛdaḥ nṛpān.

hindi: सज्जनों को, यशस्वियों को, प्रज्वलित अग्नि को, अत्यन्त स्वच्छ जलाशयों को
english: Good men (sādhu), famous (ones), a kindled fire, very clear water-bodies (jalāśaya),

text_flags.why: certain: nh for hn is a letter reversal (cf. vha/hva); vahni 'fire' is certain from the sense and the metre is unchanged

notes: GROUPING: continues the list of 42. 'yaśasvinaḥ' stands for an unstated noun, so '(ones)'.

hindi: कन्या को, कुमारों को, गोरों को, श्वेत वस्त्र वालों को, अत्यन्त तेजस्वियों को
english: A maiden, boys, fair (ones), white-clothed (ones), very radiant (ones),
notes: GROUPING: continues the list of 42. 'gaurān', 'śuklavastrān' and 'sutejasaḥ' may qualify 'kumārakān' (boys) instead of standing as separate members; read here as separate members with the unstated noun shown as '(ones)'.

hindi: नरभक्षी को, दीप्त शरीर वाले को, चारों ओर से रक्त से सींचे हुए को
english: A man-eating (one), a blazing-bodied (one), sprinkled with blood all around,
notes: GROUPING: continues the list of 42; the verb is in 46 (paśyet). The three words may describe one figure or three; the text does not say which. 'narāśana' is literally 'man-eating'; no particular being is named.

hindi: जो देखे, या जो पाता है, छत्र यानी छाता, आदर्श यानी दर्पण और अस्पष्ट शब्द विशामिष
english: He who should see, or who obtains, an umbrella (chatra), a mirror (ādarśa) and viśāmiṣa (unclear)

text_flags.why: possible: 'viśāmiṣam' does not give a clear word; ś/ṣ confusion is common, and viṣ (excrement) or viṣa (poison) with āmiṣa (flesh) are conceivable; no reading is adopted and the word is left unclear

notes: GROUPING: the list of 42-45 appears to be the object of 'paśyet' here, and the list of 46-47 of 'labhate'. 'viśāmiṣam' is left unsplit and unclear (the guesses are in the text_flag only); the first two members chatra, ādarśa are clear. The printed form 'paśyellabhate' = paśyet labhate.

hindi: श्वेत पुष्प, वस्त्र, अमेध्य यानी अशुद्ध का लेप, फल
english: White flowers (sumanas), cloth, a smearing with impure (matter), fruit,
notes: GROUPING: continues 46; these are objects of 'labhate' (obtains). 'amedhya' = unfit, impure; the substance is not named, shown as '(matter)'. 'sumanas' = flower here (it can also name jasmine; not stated).

words.gloss: mountain; palace; with fruit; tree; lion; man; elephant (dvipa, lit. 'twice-drinker')

hindi: पर्वतों, महलों, फलदार वृक्षों, सिंहों, मनुष्यों और हाथियों को
english: Mountains, palaces, fruit-bearing trees, lions, men, elephants,
notes: GROUPING: these accusatives are the objects of 'ārohet' ('should climb') in 49.

hindi: चढ़े, और घोड़े के वाहन पर, और अनुमानित पाठ पर नदों, झीलों और समुद्रों को पार करे
english: Should climb (them) and a horse-vehicle, and, on a conjectural reading, should cross rivers, lakes (hrada) and oceans (udadhi).

text_flags.why: possible: 'hada' (r dropped) and 'nadan' do not give the expected nouns; nadān hradodadhīn (rivers, lakes, oceans) fits the sense and the 8-syllable pāda; adopted on a conjectural reading

notes: GROUPING: completes the construction of 48 ('ārohet' takes 48 and the horse-vehicle). The reading 'hrada' (lake, pool) is conjectural; 'nada' (river) is the masculine word, plural 'nadān'. 'taret' is optative of √tṝ (cross, swim across).

hindi: पूर्वोत्तर दिशा से गमन, अगम्य के पास जाना, मृत्यु
english: Going by the east-north (north-east), approaching the unapproachable, death,
notes: GROUPING: 50 to 52 are further nominal items with no verb of their own; the governing verb (paśyet of 46, or syāt of 53) is not in these units, and the case forms are mixed (mṛtim accusative, niḥsṛtiḥ nominative). 'pūrvottareṇa' is the instrumental of 'east-north', i.e. the north-east direction. 'agamyāgamana' literally 'approaching the unapproachable'; in law-texts it names intercourse with a forbidden woman, which this line does not say.

words.gloss: star; mountain; radiant (ones), also the sun

hindi: संकीर्ण स्थान से निकलना, तारों, पर्वतों और प्रकाशमानों का स्पर्श
english: Emerging from a confined place, the touching of stars, mountains and radiant (ones),
notes: GROUPING: continues 50. 'bhāsvat' means radiant and is also a name of the sun; the translation keeps 'radiant (ones)'.

hindi: रोना, गिरे हुए का उठना और शत्रुओं का मर्दन यानी कुचलना
english: Weeping, the rising of one who has fallen, and the crushing of enemies,
notes: GROUPING: continues 50-51 and appears to lead into 53. 'dviṣatām' is the genitive plural participle used as a noun ('of those who hate').

hindi: जिसके लिए आयु, आरोग्य और धन हो, वह बार-बार अनुमानित पाठ पर पाता है।
english: He for whom there would be life, health (ārogya) and wealth, he often attains, on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'aśrute' (a-śrute, 'in the unheard') gives no clear sense after 'bahuśaḥ'; aśnute 'attains, enjoys' fits the sentence and the metre; adopted on a conjectural reading

notes: GROUPING: 50-53 appear to be one construction: a list of dream-events followed by this statement. The syntax is not clear: 'yasya syāt …' may mean that the listed things occur for him, with āyuḥ, ārogyam, vittam as further members, and the object of 'aśnute' is not stated. Taken in the plainest way; confidence low.

hindi: क्रुद्ध, भयभीत और कृश स्वरूप वाले पितरों, देवताओं और द्विजातियों के
english: Of forefathers (pitṛ), gods (deva) and twice-born (dvijāti) who are angry, frightened and emaciated in person,
notes: GROUPING: 54 and 55 form one sentence (54 gives the possessors, 55 the verb). 'ātman' at the end of the bahuvrīhi is read as 'in person' (the self or person of those described).

hindi: और मैले वस्त्र और फूलों वालों के भी दर्शन की प्रशंसा नहीं की जाती।
english: and of (ones) with dirty garments and flowers, the sight is not praised.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in 54; the genitive 'malina-ambara-puṣpāṇām' joins 54's list of persons by asyndeton and is rendered with 'and'.

hindi: किन्तु उन्हीं सन्तुष्टों के, शुद्ध पुष्प और वस्त्र वाले स्वरूप वालों के
english: But of those very (ones) when pleased, pure in person with flowers and garments,
notes: GROUPING: 56 and 57 form one sentence (56 gives the genitives, 57 the statement). The compound 'śuddha-puṣpa-ambara-ātman' could also mean 'of pure self, with flowers and garments'; the plainer reading is taken.

hindi: स्वप्न में दर्शन की प्रशंसा की जाती है, और उनके साथ बातचीत शुभ है।
english: the sight is praised in a dream, and conversation with them is auspicious.
notes: Completes 56. 'śasyate' (passive of √śaṃs, metre 8 syllables) is the same verb as 'praśasyate' in 55 without the prefix; not a typo. In the second clause the copula is understood.

hindi: भयंकर या शुभ स्वप्नों को देखकर, प्रातः स्नान किया हुआ, और अस्पष्ट शब्द सर्पषानमिवर्णान
english: Having seen terrible or good (śobhana) dreams, bathed in the morning, and sarpaṣānamivarṇān (unclear),

text_flags.why: certain: m for n; svapnān 'dreams' is required by the sense (cf. svapnaṃ in 40)
garbled: 'sarpaṣā' is not a form; the ending -varṇān (m. acc. pl.) is clear. A conceivable start is sarpiṣā (with ghee) or sarṣapān (mustard seeds), but no reading is adopted

notes: GROUPING: 58 and 59 form one sentence (the verb 'mucyate' is in 59). The last word is left unsplit and unclear (the guesses are in the text_flag only); its ending -varṇān is an accusative plural and may be the object of 'hutvā' in 59, which also has an accusative plural 'āktān'. 'śobhana' is read as 'good, auspicious'.

words.gloss: sesame seeds (tila, Sesamum indicum; standard; conjectural; printed tvilān)

hindi: सावित्री मन्त्र से घी में सने हुओं को या अनुमानित पाठ पर तिलों को हवन करके, पवित्र हुआ पापों से और रोगों से मुक्त हो जाता है।
english: having offered with the Sāvitrī (a sacred verse) (ones) smeared with ghee, or, on a conjectural reading, sesame seeds, purified, one is freed from sins and from diseases.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tvilān' is not a word; tilān (sesame seeds) fits an offering smeared with ghee; adopted on a conjectural reading. The double avagraha after -ā is a print habit

notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 58. The object of 'hutvā' is not clear: 'āktān' (smeared) agrees with an accusative plural, which may be the damaged word at the end of 58 or 'tilān'; the plain reading 'smeared (ones), or sesame seeds' is taken. 'sāvitryā' is the Sāvitrī verse (not further identified here). 'pūtaḥ' purified; 'mucyate' takes the instrumental. The subject is not stated ('one').

hindi: मंगल आचार से युक्त परिवार, और वैसे ही रोगी
english: The retinue endowed with auspicious conduct, and likewise the patient (ātura),
notes: GROUPING: 60 to 63 appear to be one list of signs (nominal items without verbs) ending with 63: 'that is the sign of ārogya'. The singular 'saṃpannaḥ' may qualify both retinue and patient; 'parivāra' is taken as the people around the patient. The '' in 'tathā''turaḥ' is a print habit (tathā āturaḥ).

hindi: श्रद्धावान्, अनुकूल और प्रचुर द्रव्यों के संग्रह वाला
english: Having faith, favourable, and having an abundant collection of materials (dravya),
notes: GROUPING: continues 60. 'dravya' (material, substance) is not specified further in the text.

words.gloss: sattva (a quality of mind); mark; association

hindi: सत्त्व यानी मन के गुण के लक्षणों का संयोग, वैद्यों और द्विजातियों में भक्ति
english: Association with the marks of sattva (a quality of mind), devotion to physicians and twice-born,
notes: GROUPING: continues 60-61. 'sattva' is a doctrinal term and kept; the text gives no further definition.

hindi: चिकित्सा में निराश न होना: वह आरोग्य यानी स्वास्थ्य का लक्षण है।
english: Non-despondency in treatment: that is the sign of health (ārogya).
notes: GROUPING: completes the list of 60-62; 'tad' refers to the signs just listed. Copula understood. 'a-nirveda' = absence of weariness or despair.

hindi: इस प्रकार यहाँ, क्योंकि जन्म और मरण का भली-भाँति कथन हुआ है,
english: Thus, here, since birth and death have been properly set forth,
notes: GROUPING: 64 and 65 form one sentence (yataḥ … tataḥ). 'iti' is taken as 'thus', closing the preceding statement; the alternative is that it quotes the name in 65.

hindi: इसलिए शरीर का स्थान यानी विभाग, यह शरीर कहा जाता है।
english: therefore this section (sthāna) of the body is called Śarīra (body).
notes: GROUPING: completes 64. The printed title is 'śarīra' (not śārīra) and is kept; the colophon in 67 names the section Śārīrasthāna.

words.gloss: messenger; beginning with; relating to knowledge

hindi: इस प्रकार दूतादिज्ञानीय नामक बारहवाँ अध्याय
english: Thus the twelfth chapter, named Dūtādijñānīya
notes: Colophon of the chapter. 'Dūtādijñānīya' is kept as the title (dūta-ādi-jñānīya, literally 'relating to the knowledge of the messenger and the rest').

words.gloss: illustrious; physician; lord; Siṃhagupta (name); son; illustrious; Vāgbhaṭa (name); teacher (ācārya); composed
Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha ('collection of the eight limbs'; title)

hindi: इस प्रकार वैद्यपति श्रीसिंहगुप्त के पुत्र श्रीमान् वाग्भटाचार्य द्वारा रचित अष्टाङ्गसंग्रह में दूसरा शारीरस्थान सम्पूर्ण है।
english: Thus, in the Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha composed by the illustrious teacher (ācārya) Vāgbhaṭa, son of the illustrious Siṃhagupta, lord of physicians (vaidyapati), the second Śārīrasthāna (section on the body) is complete.
notes: Colophon of the section. 'vaidya-pati' is taken as an epithet of Siṃhagupta (lord of physicians); it could also be read as part of his name. Copula understood in 'is complete'.

hindi: श्रीकृष्ण को अर्पण हो।
english: May it be an offering to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
notes: A closing dedication formula. The text does not say whether it belongs to the author or was added by the printer or scribe.
